title: Three Goals Before Halftime. Balogun's Brace at SoFi Gave America a World Cup Night to Remember.
excerpt: Folarin Balogun scored twice, Pulisic was untouchable, Gio Reyna added a stunner — and 70,000 in Inglewood watched the USMNT record their best-ever World Cup scoreline. For NRIs across the US, the tournament is in their backyard.
body:
The biggest party in American soccer history had a playlist. Katy Perry belted from the SoFi stage. LISA from Blackpink worked the crowd. Future and Anitta kept seventy thousand people on their feet. And then, as if the entertainment wasn't enough, Folarin Balogun decided to provide some of his own.

Seven minutes in, Paraguay defender Damián Bobadilla deflected a Weston McKennie cross into his own net after Christian Pulisic had danced past two defenders inside the box. The stadium — a sea of red, white, and blue in Inglewood, California — erupted with a roar that could be heard in Culver City.

The own goal was the appetizer. The main course was Balogun.

In the 31st minute, Pulisic threaded a perfect long ball through the Paraguayan backline. Balogun was wide open, and he made no mistake, slotting it past the goalkeeper. The 25-year-old forward — born in New York, raised in London, capped by the United States after switching allegiance from England — pumped his fist toward a crowd that had adopted him instantly.

Then, in first-half stoppage time, Balogun delivered his masterpiece. Receiving the ball with his back to goal, he turned and unleashed a curling strike into the top left corner that left goalkeeper Orlando Gil frozen. It was the kind of goal that gets replayed for decades. Three-nil at the break. The first American to score a World Cup brace since Bert Patenaude did it against Paraguay — yes, Paraguay — in 1930.

"It's a dreamy night," Balogun said afterward, grinning. "The reality did surpass what I envisioned." He said he would probably watch Netflix to wind down. He earned it.

The second half was a slower burn. Paraguay pulled one back through Mauricio in the 73rd minute, a reminder that they had not come to Los Angeles merely to applaud. But the Americans never looked troubled. Pochettino's men controlled possession, created chances, and absorbed pressure without breaking.

The only worry was Pulisic. The AC Milan star was substituted at halftime after taking a kick to his left calf in the first half. "Bit of a kick," he said afterward, playing it down. "I've had similar things before. Staying positive. I don't think it's anything." His status for the Australia match on June 19 in Seattle is uncertain, but for now, the USMNT is breathing easy.

The exclamation point came from the bench. Gio Reyna, who entered in the 82nd minute, scored with the last kick of the game — a gorgeous outside-of-the-foot finish that made the scoreline 4-1 and gave the United States the most goals they have ever scored in a single World Cup match.

**What NRIs in America Just Witnessed**

For the estimated 4.4 million Indian Americans spread across the country, the World Cup landing on home soil is unprecedented. Los Angeles alone has one of the largest Indian diaspora communities in the Western Hemisphere. The Bay Area gets its turn on Saturday, when Qatar plays Switzerland at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara — in the heart of Silicon Valley.

This is not a tournament happening somewhere else, on a laptop at 3 AM. The World Cup is here, in the stadiums that NRIs drive past on the way to work, in the cities where they raise their children. Friday night at SoFi was the first real proof of what that feels like: the biggest sporting event on the planet, in your backyard, with Katy Perry as the opening act.

Up next: Brazil vs Morocco in New Jersey on Saturday night. The World Cup is just getting started.

**Sources:** USA Today, Palm Beach Post, Fox Sports, FIFA
